settings.heading: No trace amounts.
settings.text: Most hair oils put just enough of a “hero” ingredient on the label to tell a good story — not enough to actually work. Here’s exactly what’s in Kehsora, and why each one earned its place.

settings.name: Rosemary
settings.text:
Rosemary has been used for centuries — not just in cooking, but as a remedy for scalp health across the Mediterranean and in Ayurveda alike. It works by improving blood circulation to the scalp, meaning hair follicles receive more of what they need to actually grow stronger.

It also carries natural antimicrobial and anti-inflammatory properties, calming an irritated or flaky scalp along the way.
settings.benefits: Scalp circulation, Follicle strength, Calms irritation
settings.best_for: Thinning, slow growth, flaky or itchy scalp
settings.pairs: Bhringraj for hair fall · Pumpkin Seed for density
settings.science:
Rosemary is the best-studied hair herb outside Ayurveda. In a 2015 randomised trial, 100 adults with pattern hair loss used either rosemary oil or 2% minoxidil for six months (Panahi et al., SKINmed). Both groups had a similar increase in hair count by month six, and the rosemary group reported less scalp itching.

Its carnosic and rosmarinic acids are strong antioxidants and calm inflammation on the scalp. The trial also shows why patience matters: little changed at three months, and the difference showed at six.
settings.how_to_use:
Blend: mix 1 part concentrate with 5 parts of your base oil — 30ml into 150ml, or 50ml into 250ml. Shake before each use.

Apply: part your hair and massage a few drops into the scalp with your fingertips for 3–5 minutes. Leave on for at least 30 minutes, or overnight, then wash.

How often: 2–3 times a week. Give it 6–12 weeks — hair grows slowly, and so do results.

Tip: rosemary is the most stimulating of the five — you may feel a gentle warmth or tingle. That's normal; if it stings, blend it more dilute.

Patch-test on the inside of your arm 24 hours before first use, and keep away from the eyes.

settings.name: Bhringraj
settings.text:
Bhringraj literally translates to “ruler of hair” in Sanskrit — a name it’s carried in classical Ayurvedic texts for thousands of years, long before “hair growth serums” existed. It’s known to stimulate hair follicles and improve scalp circulation, supporting stronger roots and reduced hair fall over time.

It’s also traditionally used to slow premature greying, and its natural cooling properties help with an overheated, stressed scalp.
settings.benefits: Reduces hair fall, Strengthens roots, Cooling & calming
settings.origin: Grows wild in damp ground across India
settings.preparation: Slow heat-infused into oil, the traditional Ayurvedic way
settings.best_for: Hair fall, weak roots, early greying, an overheated scalp
settings.pairs: Rosemary for growth · Sweet Almond for softness
settings.science:
Bhringraj — also called Keshraj, “king of hair” — appears throughout classical Ayurveda as the herb for hair and scalp. Traditionally it is cooked slowly into oil so its active compounds pass into the oil.

Modern research is early but encouraging. In a 2008 study, an Eclipta alba extract applied to the skin of rats moved hair follicles into the growth phase sooner than in untreated rats, and did better than 2% minoxidil in that test (Roy et al., Archives of Dermatological Research). Human trials are still limited, so we see it as a time-tested herb with promising science behind it — not a miracle cure.
settings.how_to_use:
Blend: mix 1 part concentrate with 5 parts of your base oil — 30ml into 150ml, or 50ml into 250ml. Shake before each use.

Apply: part your hair and massage a few drops into the scalp with your fingertips for 3–5 minutes. Leave on for at least 30 minutes, or overnight, then wash.

How often: 2–3 times a week. Give it 6–12 weeks — hair grows slowly, and so do results.

Tip: Bhringraj is cooling, which is why it is traditionally used at night. Massage it in before bed and wash in the morning.

Patch-test on the inside of your arm 24 hours before first use, and keep away from the eyes.

settings.name: Pumpkin Seed
settings.text:
Unlike our other ingredients, pumpkin seed isn’t part of ancient Ayurvedic tradition — it’s a newer addition, backed by modern research rather than centuries of folklore. It’s rich in zinc, fatty acids, and antioxidants, and some clinical studies have specifically linked it to reduced hair thinning.

Cold-pressed to preserve its natural nutrients, it’s one of the few ingredients here with real lab evidence behind it.
settings.origin: Native to the Americas; a kitchen staple across Central Europe
settings.compounds: Linoleic & oleic acids, phytosterols (beta-sitosterol), vitamin E
settings.preparation: Cold-pressed to keep its nutrients intact
settings.pairs: Rosemary for growth · Jojoba for an oily scalp
settings.science:
Pumpkin seed oil has some of the clearest human data of any natural hair ingredient. In a 24-week double-blind trial, men with pattern hair loss who took 400 mg of pumpkin seed oil daily had around 40% more hair on average, against about 10% on placebo (Cho et al., Evidence-Based Complementary and Alternative Medicine, 2014).

Researchers believe its phytosterols may help block DHT, the hormone behind pattern thinning. That trial used capsules; a 2021 study in women applying pumpkin seed oil to the scalp also reported improvement (Ibrahim et al., Journal of Cosmetic Dermatology).
settings.how_to_use:
Blend: mix 1 part concentrate with 5 parts of your base oil — 30ml into 150ml, or 50ml into 250ml. Shake before each use.

Apply: part your hair and massage a few drops into the scalp with your fingertips for 3–5 minutes. Leave on for at least 30 minutes, or overnight, then wash.

How often: 2–3 times a week. Give it 6–12 weeks — hair grows slowly, and so do results.

Tip: focus on the areas where you see thinning — the crown and the parting — and be consistent. This is a long-game ingredient.

Patch-test on the inside of your arm 24 hours before first use, and keep away from the eyes.

settings.name: Jojoba
settings.text:
Jojoba closely mimics your scalp’s own natural sebum, which means it absorbs rather than sits heavy on top — ideal for an oily scalp or anyone who finds traditional oils too greasy to use regularly. It’s naturally lightweight and non-comedogenic.

Gentle enough for daily use, it works well as both a concentrate mixed into a heavier oil, and applied directly for a fast-absorbing, non-greasy finish.
settings.origin: A desert shrub of the Sonoran Desert (Mexico and the south-western US)
settings.best_for: Oily or dandruff-prone scalps, daily use, anyone who finds oils heavy
settings.pairs: Rosemary for growth · Bhringraj for hair fall
settings.science:
Jojoba isn't really an oil at all — it's a liquid wax, made of long-chain wax esters that are remarkably similar to the wax esters in your own sebum. That likeness is why it spreads easily and sinks in instead of sitting on top.

Being a wax, it is also very stable and slow to go rancid. It rates low on comedogenic scales, so it is gentle on scalps prone to build-up, and it helps skin hold moisture without feeling greasy.
settings.how_to_use:
Blend: mix 1 part concentrate with 5 parts of your base oil — 30ml into 150ml, or 50ml into 250ml. Shake before each use.

Apply: part your hair and massage a few drops into the scalp with your fingertips for 3–5 minutes. Leave on for at least 30 minutes, or overnight, then wash.

How often: 2–3 times a week. Give it 6–12 weeks — hair grows slowly, and so do results.

Tip: because it absorbs so well, jojoba works as a light leave-in too — warm one or two drops between your palms and smooth over dry ends.

Patch-test on the inside of your arm 24 hours before first use, and keep away from the eyes.

settings.name: Sweet Almond
settings.text:
Rich in Vitamin E, sweet almond is a deeply nourishing addition formulated to soften hair, add natural shine, and strengthen strands against breakage. It’s gentle enough to work well across most hair types, including sensitive scalps.

A dependable, everyday ingredient for dry, dull, or brittle hair that needs consistent conditioning rather than an intensive treatment.
settings.benefits: Adds shine, Softens hair, Reduces breakage
settings.origin: The Mediterranean and West Asia; known in Ayurveda as badam taila
settings.compounds: Oleic & linoleic acids, vitamin E, phytosterols
settings.best_for: Dry, dull, brittle or frizzy hair; sensitive scalps
settings.pairs: Bhringraj for hair fall · Jojoba for lightness
settings.science:
Sweet almond oil is mostly oleic acid, a fatty acid that softens and lubricates the hair surface, so strands slip past each other instead of snagging and snapping. It is also naturally rich in vitamin E.

Oiling before you wash is one of the simplest ways to protect hair: a coat of oil reduces how much water each strand soaks up and swells, and repeated swelling and drying is a common cause of damage. In Ayurveda, almond oil — badam taila — has long been a favourite for head massage.
settings.how_to_use:
Blend: mix 1 part concentrate with 5 parts of your base oil — 30ml into 150ml, or 50ml into 250ml. Shake before each use.

Apply: part your hair and massage a few drops into the scalp with your fingertips for 3–5 minutes. Leave on for at least 30 minutes, or overnight, then wash.

How often: 2–3 times a week. Give it 6–12 weeks — hair grows slowly, and so do results.

Tip: run what's left on your fingers through the lengths and ends — that's where dryness shows first. Avoid if you have a tree-nut allergy.

Patch-test on the inside of your arm 24 hours before first use, and keep away from the eyes.

settings.text: Every generic oil on the market is a broad-spectrum guess. Kehsora is built the opposite way — real, potent ingredients, chosen for exactly what they do, infused properly rather than diluted for a label.
